Recommended Highlights This Week

1. GREEN-HOUSE Festival – 28–30 August, Temasek Shophouse

2. Singapore Night Festival – second weekend, 28–30 August

3. Village Encounters @ Holland Village – 29–30 August

4. A Date with Tradition – second weekend, 28–29 August

5. Singapore Gallery Month 2026 continues – through 13 September

6. Hungry Ghost Festival – Ghost Day falls 27 August

F&B Promotions

Current dining promotions across our Shangri-La Group properties in Singapore:

Shangri-La Singapore

Beng Hiang brings nearly 48 years of Hokkien heritage to the Garden Terrace, with recipes passed down from the original Chinatown shophouse. Signatures worth flagging to guests include Orh Nee (yam paste dessert) and Hae Bee Hiam (spicy dried shrimp sambal) – dishes that rarely appear on hotel menus outside a genuine Hokkien kitchen.

  • Beng Hiang – Authentic Hokkien Cuisine, Garden Terrace. Nearly 48-year-old recipes from the original Chinatown shophouse.

Shangri-La Rasa Sentosa

  • Rasa Private Beach BBQ – SGD 188++ per package (2 adults + 2 children). Valid through 31 December 2026.

Hotel Jen Tanglin

J65's Turkish guest-chef theme concludes at the end of August – worth a last-call mention before it wraps up.

  • J65: Flavours of Türkiye – from $88++/adult. Shangri-La Circle members: 20% off. Final week of August.

Hotel Jen Orchard Gateway

  • Makan@JEN – daily lunch and dinner buffet, $30–55++ per person. 15% off for OCBC cardmembers, ongoing.

Overall Summary

This week belongs to festivals: GREEN-HOUSE returns to Temasek Shophouse for its milestone fifth edition with a first-ever day-to-night format, Singapore Night Festival enters its second of three weekends with a dedicated “Legends in Motion” walking tour, and Holland Village gets its first-ever DistrictAfterDark pop-up with Village Encounters. On the heritage side, A Date with Tradition continues its second weekend at Stamford Arts Centre, and Singapore Gallery Month keeps running islandwide through mid-September. Hungry Ghost Festival also reaches its most significant date this week – Ghost Day on the 27th – so expect slightly more visible observances than in a typical week.

Events & Festivals

GREEN-HOUSE Festival

Singapore's largest experiential sustainability festival returns for its milestone fifth edition, transforming Temasek Shophouse into a hub of eco-conscious workshops, talks, marketplaces and activations. This year introduces the festival's first-ever day-to-night format, extending programming into the evening for the first time.

Event Date: 28–30 August 2026

Location: Temasek Shophouse, 28 Orchard Road

Admission: Free (some workshops may be ticketed)

Best For: Families / Sustainability-Minded Guests / Free Activities

Concierge Recommendation: A good option for guests interested in sustainability or looking for a free, low-key weekend activity right in the Orchard Road area – easy to combine with shopping.

Singapore Night Festival – Second Weekend

Singapore Night Festival continues into its second of three weekends. This week's standout is Legends in Motion, a walking tour experience presented by The Artists Village that takes guests through the Bras Basah.Bugis precinct after dark, weaving myths and legends into a moving performance rather than a fixed installation. For full background on the festival itself, see last edition.

Event Date: 28–30 August 2026 (second of three weekends; final weekend 4–5 September)

Location: Bras Basah.Bugis precinct, centred on the National Museum of Singapore

Admission: Free for most programmes

Best For: Families / Culture Seekers / Free Activities / Evening Outings

Concierge Recommendation: Still one of the best free things happening in Singapore right now – if a guest missed opening weekend, this is a good second chance, and the walking tour format offers a different experience from the static installations they may have seen photos of.

Village Encounters @ Holland Village

DistrictAfterDark launches its first-ever precinct pop-up in Holland Village, turning the neighbourhood into a festival hub packed with games, wellness activities, live music and pet-friendly programming.

Event Date: 29–30 August 2026

Location: Holland Village

Admission: Free entry. Guests who spend $30 or more at participating Holland Village merchants can redeem a complimentary Village Encounters Festival Pass (limited to the first 1,000 redemptions), unlocking a free drink, workshop access, a photobooth print and a chance to win cash vouchers

Best For: Young Adults / Couples / Pet Owners / Free Activities

Concierge Recommendation: A fun, low-key evening option for guests staying in the Holland Village / Tanglin area – mention the $30 spend threshold for the Festival Pass, since it's an easy way to add value to a dinner they were having anyway.

A Date with Tradition – Second Weekend

Stamford Arts Centre's celebration of Singapore's multicultural heritage continues into its second of three weekends, blending traditional arts with contemporary creativity through performances, installations and hands-on workshops – including Chinese calligraphy, gamelan storytelling, batik ink rubbing, a Kathakali-inspired retelling of Journey to the West, and an interactive light installation that responds to touch and movement.

Event Date: Fridays and Saturdays, 28–29 August 2026 (second of three weekends from 21 August)

Location: Stamford Arts Centre

Best For: Culture Seekers / Families / Something Different

Concierge Recommendation: A strong pick for guests wanting a genuine cultural experience rather than a purely commercial event – the hands-on workshops make it especially good for families.

adidas Orchard Ignition – Road Closure Notice

A two-day activation by adidas, the Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team and K-pop group BABYMONSTER takes over Orchard Road ahead of the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix 2026. The centrepiece, on 30 August, is Singapore's first live F1 race car demonstration in over a decade – Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS reserve driver Fred Vesti will drive an F1 car along Orchard Road, with the official closure covering the stretch from Scotts Road to Bideford Road (per LTA), with BABYMONSTER leading the flag-off ceremony and joining for Hot Laps in a Mercedes-AMG car. This requires a road closure along that stretch of Orchard Road. The evening continues with a free Fan Festival at Design Orchard (6:35pm–9:00pm) featuring Benjamin Kheng, Iman Fandi and DJ KIARA.

Event Date: 29–30 August 2026 (main road closure and demo on the 30th)

Location: Orchard Road, closure from Scotts Road to Bideford Road, 10:00am–8:30pm on 30 August (per LTA); plus adidas Brand Centre Orchard and Design Orchard

Admission: Free to view; VIP viewing decks reserved for contest winners

Expected Attendance: 30,000+ fans

Best For: Motorsport Fans / K-pop Fans / Free Activities

Concierge Recommendation: This is a genuine road closure, not just a busy day – guests staying near Paragon, ION Orchard or Tang Plaza should be warned in advance, especially those with dinner reservations or transport planned through that stretch on the 30th. Expect very heavy pedestrian crowds along the rest of Orchard Road as well.

Restaurants & Bars

Special Mention: From Shangri-La's Restaurant Recommendation List

Two picks this week from Shangri-La Singapore's own curated list of recommended restaurants across the city – no separate new opening to feature, so the spotlight goes entirely to the rotation this edition:

Tiffin Room

Part of Raffles Singapore's history since 1892, Tiffin Room serves North Indian cuisine inspired by the royal culinary heritage of the maharajahs, whose golden age coincided with the restaurant's own origins. Chef Kuldeep Negi, at the helm for almost a decade, presents specialties served tableside in traditional tiffin boxes, with spices freshly ground as part of the presentation. The restored interior reinstates wooden floorboards based on research by heritage consultants, recreating the room's early-1900s character.

Current Promotion: None advertised – check for seasonal festive set menus.

Reservation Policy: Reservations recommended; no credit card required to book.

Hours: Lunch 12:00pm–1:30pm (last seating); Dinner 6:30pm–9:00pm (last seating)

Contact: +65 6412 1244 / singapore@raffles.com

Address: Grand Lobby, Raffles Singapore, 1 Beach Road, Singapore 189673

Dress Code: Casual Chic – collared shirts and trousers for gentlemen; slip-ons and flip-flops not permitted

Concierge Recommendation: A genuinely historic dining experience, not just a themed one – worth framing to guests as one of Raffles' original restaurants rather than just “Indian food at the hotel.”

National Kitchen by Violet Oon

Housed on the second floor of the former City Hall building, now part of the National Gallery Singapore, National Kitchen showcases Singapore's own culinary heritage through the lens of Violet Oon, one of the country's best-known culinary ambassadors. The handsome, panelled 1920s-style dining room provides an elegant backdrop for a menu built around Peranakan and local flavours.

Current Promotion: None advertised.

Reservation Policy: Reservations recommended; takeaway orders can be placed by phone at least 45 minutes before pick-up.

Hours: Daily, 12:00pm–5:00pm & 6:00pm–10:30pm

Contact: +65 9834 9935

Address: 1 St Andrew's Road, #02-01, National Gallery Singapore (City Hall Wing), Singapore 178957 – enter via Coleman Street

Concierge Recommendation: A strong, easy pairing with a National Gallery visit – the Beef Rendang and Cod in Creamy Laksa Sauce are consistently well-reviewed if guests want a specific recommendation.

Hotel & Hospitality News

No new hotel or leadership announcements to report this week – all previously featured properties remain unchanged. Colleagues should continue monitoring for updates ahead of NoMad Singapore's late-2026 opening.

Transport & Operational Updates

Orchard Road Closure – adidas Orchard Ignition

Orchard Road will close from Scotts Road to Bideford Road, 10:00am–8:30pm on 30 August (per LTA), for a live F1 race car demonstration as part of adidas Orchard Ignition – see Events & Festivals for full details. Expect very heavy pedestrian crowds along the wider Orchard Road stretch on both 29 and 30 August, with over 30,000 fans expected.

Hungry Ghost Festival – Ghost Day

Ghost Day itself falls on 27 August this year – the most significant date in the seventh lunar month, when observances are traditionally at their peak. Guests may notice more incense, joss paper offerings and getai performances than on a typical day this week. This does not affect transport or access; see Edition 007 for full background on the festival's origins if the team needs a refresher.

Bras Basah.Bugis & Orchard Road Crowds

Expect heavier foot traffic around Bras Basah.Bugis (Singapore Night Festival) and Orchard Road / Temasek Shophouse (GREEN-HOUSE Festival) over the weekend of 28–30 August, as both events draw crowds into the evening.

Downtown Line Return to Normal Hours

The Downtown Line's Friday night early closures and Saturday late starts, which have been running since 10 July, are scheduled to end by 5 September. Services should return to normal hours from this point – confirm with LTA channels closer to the date.

Changi Airport Travel Advisory

Airport traffic remains elevated through the peak August travel period. Morning and weekend flights need extra buffer time for check-in, immigration and bag drop.

Looking Ahead

Singapore Night Festival – Final Weekend

The festival's third and final weekend falls 4–5 September – worth one last mention in the next edition before it wraps up for the year.

Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix Season Build-Up

Community fan events continue in the lead-up to the Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix 2026, including stops at HDB Hub, Toa Payoh (Spanish Grand Prix, 12–13 September) and Kampung Admiralty (Azerbaijan Grand Prix, 25–26 September). Worth monitoring as the race weekend itself approaches later in the year.

Additional Information

Concierge Notes

  • Ghost Day (27 August) is the peak day for Hungry Ghost Festival observances this year – a good day to proactively mention the cultural context to guests rather than wait for them to ask.

  • Village Encounters' Festival Pass is capped at 1,000 redemptions – worth mentioning the $30 spend threshold clearly so guests don't miss it after the fact.

  • J65's Flavours of Türkiye promotion at Hotel Jen Tanglin ends this month – flag this as a last-call item in guest conversations.

Suggested Itineraries

Half Day — Free Weekend Evening

Evening: Singapore Night Festival at Bras Basah.Bugis – join the Legends in Motion walking tour for a different experience from a first visit.

Tip: The walking tour has a start time and route – confirm details closer to the date rather than assuming it's a walk-up experience.

Full Day — Heritage & Culture

Morning: Singapore Gallery Month – Gillman Barracks or Tanjong Pagar Distripark for gallery-hopping.

Afternoon: A Date with Tradition at Stamford Arts Centre.

Evening: Dinner at Tiffin Room or National Kitchen by Violet Oon, then GREEN-HOUSE Festival at Temasek Shophouse if guests want to end the day with something free and low-key.

Tip: Stamford Arts Centre and Raffles Singapore (Tiffin Room) are both within a short walk of each other – easy to combine without arranging transport.

2 Days — Festivals & Food

Day 1

Morning: National Gallery Singapore – lunch at National Kitchen by Violet Oon. Afternoon: Singapore Gallery Month galleries nearby. Evening: Singapore Night Festival.

Day 2

Afternoon: Orchard Road shopping, GREEN-HOUSE Festival at Temasek Shophouse. Evening: Village Encounters @ Holland Village for dinner and live music.

Tip: If guests are staying near Orchard, Day 2 requires almost no transport planning – both stops are within the same general area.

Quick Reference

Best Free Evening Activity: Singapore Night Festival (Legends in Motion)

Best Free Sustainability Pick: GREEN-HOUSE Festival

Best New Neighbourhood Event: Village Encounters @ Holland Village

Best Cultural Experience: A Date with Tradition

Best Historic Dining: Tiffin Room

Best Local Heritage Cuisine: National Kitchen by Violet Oon
